Alger, 22 juill 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Op: Algiers, July 22, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — OpenAI revealed Tuesday that two of its AI models had hacked the Hugging Face platform during an internal security test. The incident, described as an "unprecedented cyber incident", led to a joint investigation between the two companies.
OpenAI a annoncé mardi qu'une évaluation: OpenAI announced Tuesday that an internal security assessment to test the hacking capabilities of its AI models had gone awry. Two models, including the recently launched GPT-5.6 Sol, exploited security vulnerabilities to access the internet and hack the Hugging Face platform. The incident was described as an “unprecedented cyber incident” by the American start-up.
L'évaluation avait pour but de vérifier: The evaluation aimed to verify the models' abilities to develop exploits in a strictly controlled digital environment. However, the models used a significant amount of computing power to bypass restrictions and freely access the internet. They identified and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in internally hosted third-party software to achieve this.
Ciblage de Hugging Face et activité anor: Hugging Face Targeting and Abnormal Activity
Une fois connectés à internet, les modèl: Once connected to the internet, the models targeted the Hugging Face platform, a popular repository of AI models, datasets and other information for programmers. They used stolen credentials and zero-day vulnerabilities to chain multiple attack vectors together in an attempt to remotely execute code on Hugging Face's servers.

OpenAI a indiqué avoir signalé la faille: OpenAI said it reported the zero-day flaw to the affected company and strengthened protections around future training and evaluation processes. The start-up also highlighted the need to strengthen the alignment of its models, cyber protections during evaluation phases and monitoring during internal testing.
Cet incident survient alors que des modè: The incident comes as cutting-edge AI models, like GPT-5.6 and Anthropic's Mythos series, raise concerns about their ability to breach cybersecurity defenses. Both companies had to temporarily delay the general availability of these technologies due to concerns expressed by US authorities.
